# sub-event of

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:subEventOf`](gmeow-subEventOf.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/subEventOf>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/events`](../../slices/events.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

Relates an event to a larger event it is part of — a talk within a session within a conference. Transitive: a part of a part is a part ([CIDOC-CRM](../../external/ontologies.md#target-crm) P9 consists of). A specialization of the universal [`gmeow:partOf`](gmeow-partOf.md) spine. Non-simple, so kept out of all cardinality axioms.

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use for mereological event decomposition — a talk within a session within a conference — where one occurrence is genuinely PART OF a larger occurrence; the event-scoped specialization of [`gmeow:partOf`](gmeow-partOf.md).

### Avoid when

- Avoid confusing it with the TEMPORAL [`gmeow:during`](gmeow-during.md) (which only orders extents) or the SPATIAL [`gmeow:containedInLocation`](gmeow-containedInLocation.md); sub-event-of is part-whole, not mere temporal nesting or co-location.

### How to use

- Assert [`gmeow:subEventOf`](gmeow-subEventOf.md) from the smaller event to the larger; transitivity builds the decomposition closure and generic consumers read [`gmeow:partOf`](gmeow-partOf.md) by inheritance. Read [`gmeow:hasSubEvent`](gmeow-hasSubEvent.md) as its inverse.

### Examples

- ex:talk [`gmeow:subEventOf`](gmeow-subEventOf.md) ex:session.
